     1	//! Replay an `OpLog` against a `Workbook`.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): single entry point `replay_into(&OpLog, &mut
     4	//! Workbook, &FunctionRegistry) -> Result<usize, ReplayError>`. Returns the
     5	//! count of ops successfully applied; on failure, returns
     6	//! `ReplayError::At { index, kind }` carrying the position of the failing
     7	//! op and the underlying failure. The workbook is left in a partial state
     8	//! on failure (callers decide whether to discard, recover, or recompute).
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Replay semantics
    11	//!
    12	//! Each `Op` variant maps to one `Workbook` mutation:
    13	//!
    14	//! - `PutValue` → `Workbook::put_at` (after row/col bounds check).
    15	//! - `PutFormula` → `Workbook::put_formula` (text only; replay does NOT
    16	//!   re-evaluate — that's a separate step the caller drives via
    17	//!   `WorkbookRuntime::recompute_all`).
    18	//! - `ClearFormula` → `Workbook::clear_formula`.
    19	//! - `SetName` → `Workbook::set_name`. Reserved names (e.g. `AI`) surface
    20	//!   as `ReplayError::NameRejected`.
    21	//! - `AddSheet` → `Workbook::add_sheet_with_chunk_rows`.
    22	//! - `BatchCommit` → recurse on each inner op. Index reporting flattens:
    23	//!   a failure inside a BatchCommit reports the inner op's overall
    24	//!   position (current outer index + offset).
    25	//!
    26	//! ## Idempotence
    27	//!
    28	//! `replay_into` is idempotent only in the trivial sense: replaying twice
    29	//! against the same starting workbook produces the same final state IFF
    30	//! the underlying mutation methods are themselves idempotent (and they
    31	//! are — `put_at` / `put_formula` / `clear_formula` / `set_name` /
    32	//! `add_sheet` all are). Callers wanting at-most-once semantics across
    33	//! sessions track replay state themselves (Phase 5+ work).

    37	//! Passed for API symmetry with `WorkbookRuntime::new(&mut wb, &registry)`.

   213	    #[error("replay rename-column rejected at op index {index}: table {table:?} column {column:?} ({reason})")]
   214	    TableColumnRejected {
   215	        index: usize,
   216	        table: String,
   217	        column: String,
   218	        reason: &'static str,
   219	    },
   220	
   221	    /// **W5-122 (Phase 4.8.J):** `ResizeTable` op was rejected by a
   222	    /// validation rule (arithmetic mismatch, trailing-columns
   223	    /// mismatch, column-name collision, footprint overlap, etc.).
   224	    /// `reason` is a static string describing which invariant fired.
   225	    #[error("replay resize-table rejected at op index {index}: table {name:?} ({reason})")]
   226	    TableResizeRejected {
   227	        index: usize,
   228	        name: String,
   229	        reason: &'static str,
   230	    },
   231	
   232	    /// **W5-146 (Phase 4.9.J):** `Op::SetLocale` wire value didn't
   233	    /// match any known locale code. Mirrors qbook v7's
   234	    /// `QbookError::UnknownLocale` (W5-145) — a forward-compat
   235	    /// op-log file with an unrecognized locale string surfaces this
   236	    /// instead of silently substituting EnUs (closes Sonnet L-10).
   237	    /// Captures the offending string for the IDE diagnostic.
   238	    #[error("replay unknown locale at op index {index}: {found:?}")]
   239	    UnknownLocale { index: usize, found: String },
   240	
   241	    /// **W5-151 (Phase 4.9.O MEDIUM-2 closure):** `Op::SetReferenceMode`
   242	    /// wire value didn't match `A1` or `R1C1`. Per design § 4.9.J,
   243	    /// the forward-compat path captures unknown strings into
   244	    /// `ReferenceModeWire::Unknown(_)` and replay surfaces this
   245	    /// distinct error rather than letting the op silently no-op.
   246	    /// Parallels `UnknownLocale` above.
   247	    #[error("replay unknown reference mode at op index {index}: {found:?}")]
   248	    UnknownReferenceMode { index: usize, found: String },
   249	}
   250	
   251	/// Wrapper around `ql_storage::FormatTableError` that owns its strings,
   252	/// so `ReplayError` can stay `Clone + std::error::Error` without
   253	/// borrowing into the table.
   254	///
   255	/// Phase 5.2 D-1 step 3: `id` / `existing_id` / `attempted_id` are now
   256	/// `ql_storage::FormatId` (tagged tuple) rather than the pre-step-3
   257	/// `u32`. Display formatting uses the FormatId's `Debug` impl so error
   258	/// messages identify both built-in and peer-allocated custom variants.
   259	#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error)]
   260	#[non_exhaustive]
   261	pub enum FormatRejectedSource {
   262	    #[error("format id {id:?} already bound to {existing:?}, can't re-bind to {attempted:?}")]
   263	    IdCollision {
   264	        id: ql_storage::FormatId,
   265	        existing: String,
   266	        attempted: String,
   267	    },
   268	    #[error(
   269	        "format string {string:?} already at id {existing_id:?}, can't bind to id {attempted_id:?}"
   270	    )]
   271	    StringCollision {
   272	        string: String,
   273	        existing_id: ql_storage::FormatId,
   274	        attempted_id: ql_storage::FormatId,
   275	    },
   276	}
   277	
   278	impl From<ql_storage::FormatTableError> for FormatRejectedSource {
   279	    fn from(e: ql_storage::FormatTableError) -> Self {
   280	        match e {
   281	            ql_storage::FormatTableError::IdCollision {
   282	                id,
   283	                existing,
   284	                attempted,
   285	            } => FormatRejectedSource::IdCollision {
   286	                id,
   287	                existing,
   288	                attempted,
   289	            },
   290	            ql_storage::FormatTableError::StringCollision {
   291	                string,
   292	                existing_id,
   293	                attempted_id,
   294	            } => FormatRejectedSource::StringCollision {
   295	                string,
   296	                existing_id,
   297	                attempted_id,
   298	            },
   299	            _ => unreachable!(
   300	                "FormatTableError gained a variant — extend FormatRejectedSource::From"
   301	            ),
   302	        }
   303	    }
   304	}
   305	
   306	/// Replay every op in `log` against `workbook` in append order.
   307	///
   308	/// Returns the total count of ops applied on success. On failure, the
   309	/// workbook is in a partial state — `ReplayError::At { index, .. }` tells
   310	/// the caller how far replay got.
   311	///
   312	/// The `registry` parameter is held for API symmetry with `WorkbookRuntime`
   313	/// and is unused in 2A.3.a (replay persists formula text without
   314	/// re-evaluating; callers drive evaluation through `recompute_all`).
   315	pub fn replay_into(
   316	    log: &OpLog,
   317	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
   318	    _registry: &FunctionRegistry,
   319	) -> Result<usize, ReplayError> {
   320	    let mut count = 0;
   321	    for (index, op_result) in log.iter().enumerate() {
   322	        let op = op_result.map_err(|e| ReplayError::Deserialize(index, e))?;
   323	        apply_op(&op, workbook, index)?;
   324	        count += 1;
   325	    }
   326	    Ok(count)
   327	}
   328	
   329	/// Recursive helper. `index` is the op's position in the outer log (or
   330	/// the synthetic position of the enclosing BatchCommit for nested ops —
   331	/// 2A.3.a flattens by reporting the parent's index for nested failures).
   332	fn apply_op(op: &Op, workbook: &mut Workbook, index: usize) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   333	    match op {
   334	        Op::PutValue {
   335	            sheet,
   336	            row,
   337	            col,
   338	            value,
   339	        } => {
   340	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   341	            let v: Value = value
   342	                .to_value()
   343	                .map_err(|source| ReplayError::ValueDecode { index, source })?;
   344	            workbook.put_at(*sheet, *row, *col, v);
   345	            Ok(())
   346	        }
   347	        Op::PutFormula {
   348	            sheet,
   349	            row,
   350	            col,
   351	            text,
   352	        } => {
   353	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   354	            workbook.put_formula(*sheet, *row, *col, text.as_str());
   355	            Ok(())
   356	        }
   357	        Op::ClearFormula { sheet, row, col } => {
   358	            // clear_formula is idempotent on missing entries; we still
   359	            // validate bounds so a corrupted op-log can't sneak past.
   360	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   361	            workbook.clear_formula(*sheet, *row, *col);
   362	            Ok(())
   363	        }
   364	        Op::SetName {
   365	            scope,
   366	            name,
   367	            target,
   368	        } => {
   369	            let target = target
   370	                .to_target(name)
   371	                .map_err(|source| ReplayError::NamedTargetDecode { index, source })?;
   372	            match scope {
   373	                None => {
   374	                    // Workbook-scoped (historical path).
   375	                    workbook.set_name(name, target).map_err(|source| {
   376	                        ReplayError::NameRejected {
   377	                            index,
   378	                            name: name.clone(),
   379	                            source,
   380	                        }
   381	                    })?;
   382	                }
   383	                Some(sheet) => {
   384	                    // **W5-92 (Phase 4.6.D):** sheet-scoped. Validate sheet
   385	                    // first so an unknown id surfaces as InvalidSheet, not
   386	                    // a panicking out-of-bounds index.
   387	                    let sheet_count = workbook.sheet_count();
   388	                    let sheet_ref =
   389	                        workbook
   390	                            .sheet_mut(*sheet)
   391	                            .ok_or(ReplayError::InvalidSheet {
   392	                                index,
   393	                                sheet: *sheet,
   394	                                sheet_count,
   395	                            })?;
   396	                    sheet_ref.set_scoped_name(name, target).map_err(|source| {
   397	                        ReplayError::NameRejected {
   398	                            index,
   399	                            name: name.clone(),
   400	                            source,
   401	                        }
   402	                    })?;
   403	                }
   404	            }
   405	            Ok(())
   406	        }
   407	        Op::AddSheet { name, chunk_rows } => {
   408	            // **W5-93 (Phase 4.6.E closure):** route through the fallible
   409	            // `try_add_sheet_with_chunk_rows` and surface a clean
   410	            // `ReplayError::SheetNameRejected` on validation failure.
   411	            // Codex HIGH-1 flagged that the prior infallible path
   412	            // silently accepted duplicate-canonical names + reserved
   413	            // characters at the replay boundary too.
   414	            //
   415	            // **Phase 5.2 D-2 closure (2026-05-19):** auto-rename on
   416	            // duplicate-canonical-name. Phase 5 multi-peer scenario:
   417	            // peer A and peer B both call `add_sheet("S")` locally;
   418	            // each producer-side validates against its own snapshot
   419	            // (no collision visible); both emit
   420	            // `Op::AddSheet { name: "S", ... }`; merged log has both.
   421	            // First replay succeeds; second hits the duplicate guard.
   422	            // Pre-D-2 we rejected the second op (worse UX than Google
   423	            // Sheets, which auto-renames to S(2)). Now we walk
   424	            // `<name>(2)`, `<name>(3)`, … until we find a free name.
   425	            // `Empty` + `ReservedCharacter` still reject — auto-rename
   426	            // only resolves the collaboration-collision case.
   427	            let mut chosen = name.clone();
   428	            let mut suffix = 2u32;
   429	            const AUTO_RENAME_CEILING: u32 = 10_000;
   430	            loop {
   431	                match workbook.try_add_sheet_with_chunk_rows(chosen.clone(), *chunk_rows) {
   432	                    Ok(_) => return Ok(()),
   433	                    Err(ql_storage::SheetNameError::Duplicate { .. }) => {
   434	                        chosen = format!("{name}({suffix})");
   435	                        suffix += 1;
   436	                        if suffix > AUTO_RENAME_CEILING {
   437	                            // Pathological: more than 10k sheets all
   438	                            // share the same base name (impossible in
   439	                            // realistic workbooks; max sheets per
   440	                            // workbook is 65,535). Surface a clean
   441	                            // error rather than loop forever.
   442	                            return Err(ReplayError::SheetNameRejected {
   443	                                index,
   444	                                name: name.clone(),
   445	                                source: ql_storage::SheetNameError::Duplicate {
   446	                                    name: name.clone(),
   447	                                },
   448	                            });
   449	                        }
   450	                    }
   451	                    Err(other) => {
   452	                        return Err(ReplayError::SheetNameRejected {
   453	                            index,
   454	                            name: name.clone(),
   455	                            source: other,
   456	                        });
   457	                    }
   458	                }
   459	            }
   460	        }
   461	        Op::RenameSheet {
   462	            id,
   463	            old_name,
   464	            new_name,
   465	        } => {
   466	            // **W5-91 (Phase 4.6.C):** snapshot-vs-replay reconciliation
   467	            // per design § 3.3. Three cases:
   468	            //   1. Current sheet name == old_name → fresh rename; apply.
   469	            //   2. Current sheet name == new_name → already-renamed (likely
   470	            //      replay-on-top-of-snapshot where the snapshot captured
   471	            //      the post-rename state). No-op; success.
   472	            //   3. Current sheet name == neither → divergent state; treat as
   473	            //      InvalidSheet for the op-log's safety contract.
   474	            let current = workbook.sheet(*id).map(|s| s.name().to_owned()).ok_or(
   475	                ReplayError::InvalidSheet {
   476	                    index,
   477	                    sheet: *id,
   478	                    sheet_count: workbook.sheet_count(),
   479	                },
   480	            )?;
   481	            let canonical = |s: &str| ql_storage::Workbook::canonical_sheet_name(s);
   482	            let cur_c = canonical(&current);
   483	            let old_c = canonical(old_name);
   484	            let new_c = canonical(new_name);
   485	            if cur_c == new_c {
   486	                // Already renamed (snapshot-authoritative path). No-op.
   487	                Ok(())
   488	            } else if cur_c == old_c {
   489	                workbook
   490	                    .rename_sheet(*id, new_name.clone())
   491	                    .map_err(|source| ReplayError::SheetRenameRejected {
   492	                        index,
   493	                        id: *id,
   494	                        old_name: old_name.clone(),
   495	                        new_name: new_name.clone(),
   496	                        source,
   497	                    })?;
   498	                Ok(())
   499	            } else {
   500	                Err(ReplayError::SheetRenameNameMismatch {
   501	                    index,
   502	                    id: *id,
   503	                    expected: old_name.clone(),
   504	                    found: current,
   505	                })
   506	            }
   507	        }
   508	        Op::RegisterFormat { id, string } => {
   509	            // **W5-80:** route through `FormatTable::register_at` so
   510	            // collisions surface as `FormatRejected` (rather than the
   511	            // panic-on-duplicate behavior `intern` would have via the
   512	            // by_string fast path; `register_at` is the explicit-id form).
   513	            //
   514	            // Phase 5.2 D-1 step 4: `Op::RegisterFormat.id` is now
   515	            // `FormatIdWire`. Convert to `ql_storage::FormatId` via
   516	            // `to_storage()`. The pre-step-4 `legacy_from_u32` migration
   517	            // helper is no longer needed for the wire-replay path; it's
   518	            // reserved for envelope-load migration in step 5.
   519	            let fid = id.to_storage();
   520	            workbook
   521	                .formats_mut()
   522	                .register_at(fid, string.as_str())
   523	                .map_err(|e| ReplayError::FormatRejected {
   524	                    index,
   525	                    source: e.into(),
   526	                })?;
   527	            Ok(())
   528	        }
   529	        Op::SetCellFormat {
   530	            sheet,
   531	            row,
   532	            col,
   533	            id,
   534	        } => {
   535	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   536	            // **W5-80:** require the id to be registered. Catches
   537	            // producer bugs where `SetCellFormat` was emitted without
   538	            // a preceding `RegisterFormat`. `None` means clear.
   539	            if let Some(wire_id) = id {
   540	                // Phase 5.2 D-1 step 4: same wire→storage conversion.
   541	                let fid = wire_id.to_storage();
   542	                if workbook.formats().lookup(fid).is_none() {
   543	                    return Err(ReplayError::FormatNotRegistered { index, id: fid });
   544	                }
   545	                workbook
   546	                    .sheet_mut(*sheet)
   547	                    .expect("sheet validated above")
   548	                    .format_overlay_mut()
   549	                    .set(*row, *col, fid);
   550	            } else {
   551	                workbook
   552	                    .sheet_mut(*sheet)
   553	                    .expect("sheet validated above")
   554	                    .format_overlay_mut()
   555	                    .clear(*row, *col);
   556	            }
   557	            Ok(())
   558	        }
   559	        Op::BatchCommit { ops } => {
   560	            for inner_op in ops {
   561	                // Phase 2A.3.a: nested ops flatten to the parent's index
   562	                // for error reporting. Phase 5+ may extend with
   563	                // (outer, inner) tuple indexing once the producer side
   564	                // emits nested commits in practice.
   565	                apply_op(inner_op, workbook, index)?;
   566	            }
   567	            Ok(())
   568	        }
   569	        Op::CreateTable {
   570	            name,
   571	            sheet,
   572	            top_row,
   573	            top_col,
   574	            rows,
   575	            cols,
   576	            has_header,
   577	            has_totals,
   578	            column_names,
   579	        } => apply_create_table(
   580	            workbook,
   581	            index,
   582	            name,
   583	            *sheet,
   584	            *top_row,
   585	            *top_col,
   586	            *rows,
   587	            *cols,
   588	            *has_header,
   589	            *has_totals,
   590	            column_names,
   591	        ),
   592	        Op::DropTable { name } => {
   593	            let canonical = name.to_ascii_uppercase();
   594	            if workbook.tables_mut().remove(canonical.as_str()).is_none() {
   595	                return Err(ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   596	                    index,
   597	                    name: name.clone(),
   598	                });
   599	            }
   600	            Ok(())
   601	        }
   602	        Op::RenameTable { old_name, new_name } => {
   603	            apply_rename_table(workbook, index, old_name, new_name)
   604	        }
   605	        Op::RenameColumn {
   606	            table,
   607	            old_name,
   608	            new_name,
   609	        } => apply_rename_column(workbook, index, table, old_name, new_name),
   610	        Op::ResizeTable {
   611	            name,
   612	            new_rows,
   613	            new_cols,
   614	            added_columns,
   615	            removed_columns,
   616	        } => apply_resize_table(
   617	            workbook,
   618	            index,
   619	            name,
   620	            *new_rows,
   621	            *new_cols,
   622	            added_columns,
   623	            removed_columns,
   624	        ),
   625	        // **W5-146 (Phase 4.9.J) + W5-151 (4.9.O MEDIUM-2 closure):**
   626	        // workbook-scope reference-mode change. Forward-compat
   627	        // unknown wire values surface `ReplayError::UnknownReferenceMode`
   628	        // with the captured string (mirrors the `LocaleWire::Unknown`
   629	        // path below).
   630	        Op::SetReferenceMode { mode } => match mode.clone().to_runtime() {
   631	            Ok(m) => {
   632	                workbook.set_reference_mode(m);
   633	                Ok(())
   634	            }
   635	            Err(found) => Err(ReplayError::UnknownReferenceMode { index, found }),
   636	        },
   637	        // **W5-146 (Phase 4.9.J):** workbook-scope locale change.
   638	        // Unknown wire values (forward-compat op-log file) surface
   639	        // `ReplayError::UnknownLocale` with the captured string.
   640	        Op::SetLocale { locale } => match locale.clone().to_runtime() {
   641	            Ok(loc) => {
   642	                workbook.set_locale(loc);
   643	                Ok(())
   644	            }
   645	            Err(found) => Err(ReplayError::UnknownLocale { index, found }),
   646	        },
   647	    }
   648	}
   649	
   650	/// **W5-119 (Phase 4.8.I):** replay a `RenameTable`. Validates source
   651	/// exists, target name is available (TableTable + NameTable shared
   652	/// namespace), then re-keys the entry. Note: formula text rewrites
   653	/// arrive as accompanying `Op::PutFormula` ops; this arm doesn't
   654	/// touch formula cells.
   655	fn apply_rename_table(
   656	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
   657	    index: usize,
   658	    old_name: &str,
   659	    new_name: &str,
   660	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   661	    let old_canonical = old_name.to_ascii_uppercase();
   662	    let new_canonical: std::sync::Arc<str> =
   663	        std::sync::Arc::from(new_name.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str());
   664	
   665	    // Verify source.
   666	    if workbook.tables().lookup(&old_canonical).is_none() {
   667	        return Err(ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   668	            index,
   669	            name: old_name.to_owned(),
   670	        });
   671	    }
   672	    // Verify target availability (skip the no-op same-name case).
   673	    if !old_canonical.eq_ignore_ascii_case(new_name) {
   674	        if workbook.tables().lookup(&new_canonical).is_some() {
   675	            return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   676	                index,
   677	                name: new_name.to_owned(),
   678	                reason: "table with this canonical name already exists (rename target)",
   679	            });
   680	        }
   681	        if workbook.names().lookup_ci(&new_canonical).is_some() {
   682	            return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   683	                index,
   684	                name: new_name.to_owned(),
   685	                reason: "defined-name with this canonical name already exists (rename target)",
   686	            });
   687	        }
   688	    }
   689	    // Take the entry out, mutate name + display, reinsert under new key.
   690	    let mut meta = workbook
   691	        .tables_mut()
   692	        .remove(&old_canonical)
   693	        .expect("verified above");
   694	    meta.name = std::sync::Arc::clone(&new_canonical);
   695	    meta.display_name = std::sync::Arc::from(new_name);
   696	    workbook.tables_mut().insert(new_canonical, meta);
   697	    Ok(())
   698	}
   699	
   700	/// **W5-121 (Phase 4.8.I.2):** replay a `RenameColumn`. Validates the
   701	/// target table exists, the source column exists (case-insensitive), and
   702	/// the target column name is available within the table. Mutates the
   703	/// matching `TableColumn`'s `name` (lowercase canonical) and `display`
   704	/// (case-preserving). Bumps the `TableTable` generation so plan caches
   705	/// invalidate. Same-canonical column renames are rejected — the producer
   706	/// side treats those as a no-op and doesn't emit the op, so receiving
   707	/// one indicates log divergence.
   708	fn apply_rename_column(
   709	    workbook: &mut ql_storage::Workbook,
   710	    index: usize,
   711	    table: &str,
   712	    old_name: &str,
   713	    new_name: &str,
   714	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   715	    let table_canonical = table.to_ascii_uppercase();
   716	    let meta = workbook
   717	        .tables_mut()
   718	        .get_mut(&table_canonical)
   719	        .ok_or_else(|| ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   720	            index,
   721	            name: table.to_owned(),
   722	        })?;
   723	    let (col_idx, _) =
   724	        meta.lookup_column(old_name)
   725	            .ok_or_else(|| ReplayError::TableColumnNotFound {
   726	                index,
   727	                table: table.to_owned(),
   728	                column: old_name.to_owned(),
   729	            })?;
   730	    if new_name.is_empty() {
   731	        return Err(ReplayError::TableColumnRejected {
   732	            index,
   733	            table: table.to_owned(),
   734	            column: new_name.to_owned(),
   735	            reason: "column name cannot be empty",
   736	        });
   737	    }
   738	    let old_lower = old_name.to_ascii_lowercase();
   739	    let new_lower = new_name.to_ascii_lowercase();
   740	    if old_lower == new_lower {
   741	        return Err(ReplayError::TableColumnRejected {
   742	            index,
   743	            table: table.to_owned(),
   744	            column: new_name.to_owned(),
   745	            reason: "rename to same canonical column name (producer should not emit)",
   746	        });
   747	    }
   748	    if meta.lookup_column(new_name).is_some() {
   749	        return Err(ReplayError::TableColumnRejected {
   750	            index,
   751	            table: table.to_owned(),
   752	            column: new_name.to_owned(),
   753	            reason: "column with this canonical name already exists (rename target)",
   754	        });
   755	    }
   756	    meta.columns[col_idx as usize].name = std::sync::Arc::from(new_lower.as_str());
   757	    meta.columns[col_idx as usize].display = std::sync::Arc::from(new_name);
   758	    workbook.tables_mut().bump_generation();
   759	    Ok(())
   760	}
   761	
   762	/// **W5-122 (Phase 4.8.J):** replay a `ResizeTable`. Validates the
   763	/// target table exists, the arithmetic invariant
   764	/// (`new_cols == old_cols + added.len() - removed.len()`),
   765	/// `removed_columns` exactly match the current trailing columns
   766	/// (case-insensitive on display), the final column roster has unique
   767	/// canonical names, and the new footprint cells outside the old
   768	/// footprint don't overlap other tables. Mutates the table metadata
   769	/// in place (rows/cols + columns vec). Bumps `TableTable` generation.
   770	fn apply_resize_table(
   771	    workbook: &mut ql_storage::Workbook,
   772	    index: usize,
   773	    name: &str,
   774	    new_rows: u32,
   775	    new_cols: u32,
   776	    added_columns: &[String],
   777	    removed_columns: &[String],
   778	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   779	    use ql_storage::TableColumn;
   780	    let canonical = name.to_ascii_uppercase();
   781	    // Snapshot the immutable bits we need to validate before mutating.
   782	    let (sheet, top_row, top_col, old_rows, old_cols, old_displays) = {
   783	        let meta =
   784	            workbook
   785	                .tables()
   786	                .lookup(&canonical)
   787	                .ok_or_else(|| ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   788	                    index,
   789	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   790	                })?;
   791	        (
   792	            meta.sheet,
   793	            meta.top_row,
   794	            meta.top_col,
   795	            meta.rows,
   796	            meta.cols,
   797	            meta.columns
   798	                .iter()
   799	                .map(|c| c.display.as_ref().to_owned())
   800	                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   801	        )
   802	    };
   803	    if new_rows == 0 || new_cols == 0 {
   804	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   805	            index,
   806	            name: name.to_owned(),
   807	            reason: "table rows and cols must both be > 0",
   808	        });
   809	    }
   810	    // **W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 — Codex HIGH-1):** validate footprint
   811	    // upper bound mirrors producer side.
   812	    if let Err(reason) =
   813	        ql_storage::TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds(top_row, top_col, new_rows, new_cols)
   814	    {
   815	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   816	            index,
   817	            name: name.to_owned(),
   818	            reason,
   819	        });
   820	    }
   821	    let added_len = added_columns.len() as u32;
   822	    let removed_len = removed_columns.len() as u32;
   823	    if removed_len > old_cols {
   824	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   825	            index,
   826	            name: name.to_owned(),
   827	            reason: "removed_columns count exceeds existing column count",
   828	        });
   829	    }
   830	    // Arithmetic invariant.
   831	    if new_cols != old_cols + added_len - removed_len {
   832	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   833	            index,
   834	            name: name.to_owned(),
   835	            reason: "new_cols does not match old_cols + added - removed",
   836	        });
   837	    }
   838	    // removed_columns must exactly match trailing displays
   839	    // (case-insensitive).
   840	    let trailing_start = (old_cols - removed_len) as usize;
   841	    for (i, expected) in removed_columns.iter().enumerate() {
   842	        let idx = trailing_start + i;
   843	        if !old_displays[idx].eq_ignore_ascii_case(expected) {
   844	            return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   845	                index,
   846	                name: name.to_owned(),
   847	                reason: "removed_columns do not match trailing columns",
   848	            });
   849	        }
   850	    }
   851	    // added_columns: non-empty + unique vs final roster.
   852	    if added_columns.iter().any(|s| s.is_empty()) {
   853	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   854	            index,
   855	            name: name.to_owned(),
   856	            reason: "added column names cannot be empty",
   857	        });
   858	    }
   859	    // Build the final canonical (lowercase) roster.
   860	    let mut final_canon: Vec<String> = old_displays
   861	        .iter()
   862	        .take(trailing_start)
   863	        .map(|d| d.to_ascii_lowercase())
   864	        .collect();
   865	    for a in added_columns {
   866	        final_canon.push(a.to_ascii_lowercase());
   867	    }
   868	    {
   869	        use std::collections::HashSet;
   870	        let mut seen: HashSet<&str> = HashSet::new();
   871	        for cn in &final_canon {
   872	            if !seen.insert(cn.as_str()) {
   873	                return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   874	                    index,
   875	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   876	                    reason: "final column roster has duplicate canonical names",
   877	                });
   878	            }
   879	        }
   880	    }
   881	    // Footprint-overlap check: only cells NEWLY claimed by this resize
   882	    // need checking. Old-footprint cells already belong to this table.
   883	    // We test all cells in [top_row..top_row+new_rows] x [top_col..
   884	    // top_col+new_cols] and skip those inside the OLD footprint.
   885	    let old_end_row = top_row + old_rows;
   886	    let old_end_col = top_col + old_cols;
   887	    let new_end_row = top_row + new_rows;
   888	    let new_end_col = top_col + new_cols;
   889	    for r in top_row..new_end_row {
   890	        for c in top_col..new_end_col {
   891	            let inside_old = r < old_end_row && c < old_end_col;
   892	            if inside_old {
   893	                continue;
   894	            }
   895	            if let Some(other) = workbook.table_at(sheet, r, c) {
   896	                if !other.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&canonical) {
   897	                    return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   898	                        index,
   899	                        name: name.to_owned(),
   900	                        reason: "new footprint overlaps an existing table",
   901	                    });
   902	                }
   903	            }
   904	            // **W5-124 (Phase 4.8.J.2):** spill-anchor check mirrors
   905	            // producer side. Per design § 4.3 invariant #5, tables
   906	            // block ALL spill anchors inside their footprint.
   907	            if workbook.spill_anchor_at(sheet, r, c).is_some() {
   908	                return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   909	                    index,
   910	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   911	                    reason: "new footprint contains a spill anchor",
   912	                });
   913	            }
   914	        }
   915	    }
   916	    // ----- Mutation -----
   917	    // Allocate new column ids BEFORE taking &mut on the table entry
   918	    // (allocate_column_id lives on TableTable not TableMetadata).
   919	    let new_ids: Vec<u32> = (0..added_columns.len())
   920	        .map(|_| workbook.tables_mut().allocate_column_id())
   921	        .collect();
   922	    let meta = workbook
   923	        .tables_mut()
   924	        .get_mut(&canonical)
   925	        .expect("verified at top");
   926	    meta.rows = new_rows;
   927	    meta.cols = new_cols;
   928	    meta.columns
   929	        .truncate(meta.columns.len() - removed_len as usize);
   930	    for (cn, id) in added_columns.iter().zip(new_ids) {
   931	        meta.columns.push(TableColumn {
   932	            id,
   933	            name: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str()),
   934	            display: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.as_str()),
   935	            totals_function: None,
   936	        });
   937	    }
   938	    workbook.tables_mut().bump_generation();
   939	    Ok(())
   940	}
   941	
   942	/// **W5-118 (Phase 4.8.H):** apply a `CreateTable` op against the
   943	/// workbook. Validates the same invariants the producer side checks
   944	/// (mirror via `WorkbookRuntime::create_table`).
   945	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   946	fn apply_create_table(
   947	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
   948	    index: usize,
   949	    name: &str,
   950	    sheet: SheetId,
   951	    top_row: RowId,
   952	    top_col: ColId,
   953	    rows: u32,
   954	    cols: u32,
   955	    has_header: bool,
   956	    has_totals: bool,
   957	    column_names: &[String],
   958	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   959	    use ql_storage::{TableColumn, TableMetadata};
   960	    let canonical: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(name.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str());
   961	    if workbook.tables().lookup(&canonical).is_some() {
   962	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   963	            index,
   964	            name: name.to_owned(),
   965	            reason: "table with this canonical name already exists",
   966	        });
   967	    }
   968	    if workbook.names().lookup_ci(&canonical).is_some() {
   969	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   970	            index,
   971	            name: name.to_owned(),
   972	            reason: "defined-name with this canonical name already exists (shared namespace)",
   973	        });
   974	    }
   975	    if column_names.len() != cols as usize {
   976	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   977	            index,
   978	            name: name.to_owned(),
   979	            reason: "column_names length does not match cols",
   980	        });
   981	    }
   982	    if column_names.iter().any(|s| s.is_empty()) {
   983	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   984	            index,
   985	            name: name.to_owned(),
   986	            reason: "table column names cannot be empty",
   987	        });
   988	    }
   989	    // Column-name uniqueness (case-insensitive).
   990	    {
   991	        use std::collections::HashSet;
   992	        let mut seen: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
   993	        for cn in column_names {
   994	            if !seen.insert(cn.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
   995	                return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   996	                    index,
   997	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   998	                    reason: "table column names must be unique (case-insensitive)",
   999	                });
  1000	            }
  1001	        }
  1002	    }
  1003	    if workbook.sheet(sheet).is_none() {
  1004	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1005	            index,
  1006	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1007	            reason: "table references unknown sheet",
  1008	        });
  1009	    }
  1010	    if rows == 0 || cols == 0 {
  1011	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1012	            index,
  1013	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1014	            reason: "table rows and cols must both be > 0",
  1015	        });
  1016	    }
  1017	    // **W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 — Codex HIGH-1):** validate footprint
  1018	    // upper bound mirrors producer side.
  1019	    if let Err(reason) =
  1020	        ql_storage::TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds(top_row, top_col, rows, cols)
  1021	    {
  1022	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1023	            index,
  1024	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1025	            reason,
  1026	        });
  1027	    }
  1028	    // Non-overlap + no-spill-anchor inside the footprint.
  1029	    // **W5-124 (Phase 4.8.J.2):** spill-anchor check mirrors producer
  1030	    // side per design § 4.3 invariant #5.
  1031	    for r in top_row..top_row + rows {
  1032	        for c in top_col..top_col + cols {
  1033	            if workbook.table_at(sheet, r, c).is_some() {
  1034	                return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1035	                    index,
  1036	                    name: name.to_owned(),
  1037	                    reason: "table footprint overlaps an existing table",
  1038	                });
  1039	            }
  1040	            if workbook.spill_anchor_at(sheet, r, c).is_some() {
  1041	                return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1042	                    index,
  1043	                    name: name.to_owned(),
  1044	                    reason: "table footprint contains a spill anchor",
  1045	                });
  1046	            }
  1047	        }
  1048	    }
  1049	    // Build columns with freshly-allocated ids.
  1050	    let columns: Vec<TableColumn> = column_names
  1051	        .iter()
  1052	        .map(|cn| TableColumn {
  1053	            id: workbook.tables_mut().allocate_column_id(),
  1054	            name: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str()),
  1055	            display: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.as_str()),
  1056	            totals_function: None,
  1057	        })
  1058	        .collect();
  1059	    let meta = TableMetadata {
  1060	        name: canonical.clone(),
  1061	        display_name: std::sync::Arc::from(name),
  1062	        sheet,
  1063	        top_row,
  1064	        top_col,
  1065	        rows,
  1066	        cols,
  1067	        has_header,
  1068	        has_totals,
  1069	        columns,
  1070	    };
  1071	    workbook.tables_mut().insert(canonical, meta);
  1072	    Ok(())
  1073	}
  1074	
  1075	fn validate_cell(
  1076	    workbook: &Workbook,
  1077	    sheet: SheetId,
  1078	    row: RowId,
  1079	    col: ColId,
  1080	    index: usize,
  1081	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
  1082	    let count = workbook.sheet_count();
  1083	    if (sheet as usize) >= count {
  1084	        return Err(ReplayError::InvalidSheet {
  1085	            index,
  1086	            sheet,
  1087	            sheet_count: count,
  1088	        });
  1089	    }
  1090	    if row > MAX_ROW {
  1091	        return Err(ReplayError::InvalidCell {
  1092	            index,
  1093	            row,
  1094	            col,
  1095	            why: "row exceeds MAX_ROW (1,048,575)",
  1096	        });
  1097	    }
  1098	    if col > MAX_COLUMN {
  1099	        return Err(ReplayError::InvalidCell {
  1100	            index,
  1101	            row,
  1102	            col,
  1103	            why: "col exceeds MAX_COLUMN (16,383)",
  1104	        });
  1105	    }
  1106	    Ok(())
  1107	}

  1666	            name: "S2".to_owned(),

  1669	        .unwrap();
  1670	        log.append(Op::PutFormula {

  1673	            col: 0,
  1674	            text: "S1!A1 + 1".to_owned(),
  1675	        })
  1676	        .unwrap();
  1677	        log.append(Op::BatchCommit {
  1678	            ops: vec![
  1679	                Op::PutFormula {
  1680	                    sheet: 1,
  1681	                    row: 0,
  1682	                    col: 0,
  1683	                    text: "SX!A1 + 1".to_owned(),

  1687	                    old_name: "S1".to_owned(),

  1691	        })
  1692	        .unwrap();
  1693	
  1694	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1695	        let reg = default_registry();
  1696	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap();
  1697	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "SX");
  1698	        assert_eq!(
  1699	            wb.formula_at(1, 0, 0).map(|s| s.as_ref().to_owned()),

  1803	    // ===== W5-93 (Phase 4.6.E closure) Op::AddSheet name validation =====
  1804	
  1805	    #[test]
  1806	    fn replay_add_sheet_canonical_duplicate_auto_renames() {
  1807	        // **Phase 5.2 D-2 closure (2026-05-19):** auto-rename replaces
  1808	        // the pre-D-2 behavior of rejecting duplicate-canonical names
  1809	        // at replay. Phase 5 collaboration scenario: peer A and peer B
  1810	        // both call `add_sheet("Sheet1")` locally with no collision
  1811	        // visible at producer time; both append the op; merged log
  1812	        // has both. Per the Google Sheets / Excel Online pattern, the
  1813	        // second auto-renames to `Sheet1(2)` rather than rejecting.
  1814	        //
  1815	        // Pre-D-2 this test was `replay_add_sheet_canonical_duplicate_rejected`
  1816	        // asserting `ReplayError::SheetNameRejected`. The D-2 spec
  1817	        // (5.1 audit Opus H-3) inverted that expectation.
  1818	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1819	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1820	            name: "Sheet1".to_owned(),
  1821	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1822	        })
  1823	        .unwrap();
  1824	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1825	            name: "SHEET1".to_owned(),
  1826	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1827	        })
  1828	        .unwrap();
  1829	
  1830	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1831	        let reg = default_registry();
  1832	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).expect("auto-rename succeeds");
  1833	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet_count(), 2);
  1834	        // First sheet keeps its name.
  1835	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1");
  1836	        // Second sheet auto-renamed (original was "SHEET1" which is
  1837	        // a canonical-duplicate of "Sheet1"; suffix starts at (2)).
  1838	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(1).unwrap().name(), "SHEET1(2)");
  1839	    }
  1840	
  1841	    #[test]
  1842	    fn replay_add_sheet_auto_rename_walks_suffix_until_free() {
  1843	        // Three peers concurrently add "Sheet1"; replay should
  1844	        // produce Sheet1, Sheet1(2), Sheet1(3).
  1845	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1846	        for _ in 0..3 {
  1847	            log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1848	                name: "Sheet1".to_owned(),
  1849	                chunk_rows: 16,

  1851	            .unwrap();
  1852	        }
  1853	
  1854	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1855	        let reg = default_registry();
  1856	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap();
  1857	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet_count(), 3);
  1858	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1");
  1859	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(1).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1(2)");
  1860	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(2).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1(3)");
  1861	    }

    76	/// Wire-format mirror of `ql_types::Value`. Phase 1 W5-6 doesn't add Serialize to

    79	///
    80	/// Phase 2A.8 (megaudit M11): added `Pending` variant for formula-bearing cells
    81	/// whose saved value would be `Value::Blank` (because the formula hasn't been
    82	/// evaluated yet, or its result really is Blank). Previously this case was
    83	/// encoded as `Error("#NULL!")`, conflating "not yet evaluated" with a real
    84	/// Excel `#NULL!` error. The v2 reader recognizes `Pending` as "needs
    85	/// recompute"; for v1 files, the loader auto-rewrites `Error(#NULL!)` to
    86	/// `Pending` when the same cell has a `formula` field.

    90	    Boolean(bool),
    91	    Text(String),
    92	    /// Stored as the canonical "#REF!" / "#VALUE!" / etc. text form.
    93	    Error(String),
    94	    /// Formula-bearing cell with no evaluated value. Recompute resolves it.
    95	    Pending,
    96	}

    98	impl CellWireValue {
    99	    /// Project a runtime `Value` into the wire shape, or `None` for `Blank`
   100	    /// (which is encoded as the absence of a `CellRecord` entry on disk).
   101	    pub fn from_value(v: &Value) -> Option<Self> {
   102	        match v {
   103	            Value::Blank => None,
   104	            Value::Number(n) => Some(CellWireValue::Number(*n)),
   105	            Value::Boolean(b) => Some(CellWireValue::Boolean(*b)),
   106	            Value::Text(s) => Some(CellWireValue::Text(s.as_ref().to_owned())),

   157	    /// Project a runtime `NamedTarget` into the wire shape for serialization.
   158	    pub fn from_target(t: &NamedTarget) -> Self {

   161	                sheet: addr.sheet,
   162	                row: addr.row,
   163	                col: addr.col,

   175	                // Error("BLANK_SENTINEL")? Also wrong. The cleanest answer: refuse

   177	                // and we'd round-trip-lose it anyway.
   178	                //

   254	/// Wire-format mirror of the (forthcoming) `ql_storage::FormatId` tagged
   255	/// tuple introduced in **Phase 5.2 D-1 step 3**. Step 2 (2026-05-19) ships
   256	/// this wire type ahead of the storage-side change; step 4 wires it into
   257	/// `Op::RegisterFormat` / `Op::SetCellFormat`.
   258	///
   259	/// Two variants:
   260	/// - `Builtin { id }` — Excel-canonical built-in format ids (0..=163).
   261	///   Stable across peers; no merge collisions possible.
   262	/// - `Custom { peer, counter }` — peer-allocated custom format ids.
   263	///   Each peer's allocator increments its own `counter`; concurrent
   264	///   peers can't collide because `peer` differs.
   265	///
   266	/// Serde shape is `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]`,
   267	/// mirroring `NamedTargetWire`: self-describing JSON for schema
   268	/// robustness in the `.qbook` envelope. `peer` is a raw `u64`
   269	/// (`PeerId` is `#[serde(transparent)]`).
   270	///
   271	/// ```text
   272	/// {"kind": "builtin", "id": 14}
   273	/// {"kind": "custom", "peer": 42, "counter": 7}
   274	/// ```
   275	///
   276	/// The collision-freedom guarantee (Phase 5.1 audit-locked decision D-1)
   277	/// comes from the `Custom` variant carrying the originating peer's id:
   278	/// two concurrent peers with distinct `peer` values can both allocate
   279	/// `counter = 0` without colliding because the full `FormatId` differs
   280	/// in its `peer` component.

   282	#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase", deny_unknown_fields)]
   283	pub enum FormatIdWire {
   284	    Builtin { id: u32 },
   285	    Custom { peer: PeerId, counter: u32 },
   286	}
   287	
   288	/// First xlsx custom-format `numFmtId`, mirroring Excel + OpenFormula
   289	/// conventions. Built-in format ids occupy `0..=FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX`;
   290	/// custom format ids start at `FIRST_XLSX_CUSTOM_NUMFMT = 164`. Pre-5.2
   291	/// `.qbook` saves used this boundary to allocate single-writer custom
   292	/// ids; the step-5 envelope-migration `from_u32_legacy` reads it back.
   293	const FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX: u32 = 163;

   295	impl FormatIdWire {
   296	    /// **Phase 5.2 D-1 step 2 migration helper (born here, used by step
   297	    /// 5's qbook envelope loader):** map a pre-5.2 bare-`u32` `FormatId`
   298	    /// encoding to the new tagged-tuple wire shape.
   299	    ///
   300	    /// Pre-5.2 encoding: `FormatId` was `pub struct FormatId(pub u32)`.
   301	    /// Values `0..=FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX` are Excel-canonical built-in
   302	    /// format ids. Values `>= FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX + 1` were allocated
   303	    /// by the engine's single-writer custom counter, starting at
   304	    /// `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX + 1 = 164`.
   305	    ///
   306	    /// Migration mapping:
   307	    /// - `n <= 163` → `Builtin { id: n }`.
   308	    /// - `n >= 164` → `Custom { peer: LEGACY_PEER, counter: n - 164 }`.
   309	    ///
   310	    /// `LEGACY_PEER = PeerId(0)` is the sentinel for "this custom id
   311	    /// was allocated by a pre-collab single-writer save"; per Phase

   313	    /// peer-id 0, so legacy ids can't collide with custom ids allocated
   314	    /// by an active session.
   315	    pub fn from_u32_legacy(n: u32) -> Self {

   317	            FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: n }

   319	            FormatIdWire::Custom {
   320	                peer: LEGACY_PEER,
   321	                counter: n - (FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX + 1),
   322	            }
   323	        }
   324	    }

   342	        match self {

   358	    Some(match s {

   379	mod format_id_wire_tests {
   380	    //! Phase 5.2 D-1 step 2 (2026-05-19): tests for `FormatIdWire`.
   381	    //!
   382	    //! Pre-step-2 the only `FormatId` shape was `u32`. Step 2 introduces
   383	    //! the wire-side tagged tuple; storage-side change lands in step 3.
   384	    //! Tests pin:
   385	    //! - Serde round-trips for both variants (no drift in JSON shape
   386	    //!   over future Loro/serde upgrades).
   387	    //! - `from_u32_legacy` migration boundaries (0, 163, 164, large).
   388	    //! - Equality + Hash semantics (these matter for HashMap keying
   389	    //!   in step 3's `FormatTable`).
   390	    use super::*;
   391	    use std::collections::HashSet;
   392	
   393	    #[test]
   394	    fn builtin_round_trips_through_json() {
   395	        let original = FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: 14 };
   396	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&original).unwrap();
   397	        assert_eq!(json, r#"{"kind":"builtin","id":14}"#);
   398	        let back: FormatIdWire = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
   399	        assert_eq!(back, original);
   400	    }
   401	
   402	    #[test]
   403	    fn custom_round_trips_through_json() {
   404	        let original = FormatIdWire::Custom {
   405	            peer: PeerId::new(42),
   406	            counter: 7,
   407	        };
   408	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&original).unwrap();
   409	        // `peer` is serde-transparent, so it appears as a bare u64.
   410	        assert_eq!(json, r#"{"kind":"custom","peer":42,"counter":7}"#);
   411	        let back: FormatIdWire = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
   412	        assert_eq!(back, original);
   413	    }
   414	
   415	    #[test]
   416	    fn from_u32_legacy_maps_zero_to_builtin() {
   417	        // Lower boundary: `0` is the General format (built-in id 0).
   418	        assert_eq!(
   419	            FormatIdWire::from_u32_legacy(0),
   420	            FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: 0 }
   421	        );
   422	    }
   423	
   424	    #[test]
   425	    fn from_u32_legacy_maps_163_to_builtin() {
   426	        // Upper boundary of built-in range. Excel's last built-in is 163.
   427	        assert_eq!(
   428	            FormatIdWire::from_u32_legacy(163),
   429	            FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: 163 }
   430	        );
   431	    }
   432	
   433	    #[test]
   434	    fn from_u32_legacy_maps_164_to_custom_counter_zero() {
   435	        // First legacy custom id. counter starts at 0 (n - 164).
   436	        assert_eq!(
   437	            FormatIdWire::from_u32_legacy(164),
   438	            FormatIdWire::Custom {
   439	                peer: LEGACY_PEER,
   440	                counter: 0,
   441	            }
   442	        );
   443	    }
   444	
   445	    #[test]
   446	    fn from_u32_legacy_maps_large_to_custom() {
   447	        // Arbitrary mid-range legacy custom id.
   448	        assert_eq!(
   449	            FormatIdWire::from_u32_legacy(999),
   450	            FormatIdWire::Custom {
   451	                peer: LEGACY_PEER,
   452	                counter: 999 - 164,
   453	            }
   454	        );
   455	    }
   456	
   457	    #[test]
   458	    fn equality_and_hash_consistent_across_variants() {
   459	        // Two Builtin(14) are equal + hash-equal; Builtin(14) and
   460	        // Custom(LEGACY_PEER, 0) (legacy-mapped from u32=164) are NOT
   461	        // equal even though the latter encodes the same xlsx numFmtId
   462	        // pre-migration. Step 5's loader is responsible for not mixing
   463	        // pre- and post-migration ids in the same workbook.
   464	        let a = FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: 14 };
   465	        let b = FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: 14 };
   466	        let c = FormatIdWire::Custom {
   467	            peer: LEGACY_PEER,
   468	            counter: 0,
   469	        };
   470	        assert_eq!(a, b);
   471	        assert_ne!(a, c);
   472	        let mut set: HashSet<FormatIdWire> = HashSet::new();
   473	        set.insert(a);
   474	        assert!(set.contains(&b));
   475	        assert!(!set.contains(&c));
   476	    }
   477	
   478	    #[test]
   479	    fn distinct_peers_with_same_counter_dont_collide() {
   480	        // Phase 5.1 audit-locked decision D-1: collision-freedom relies
   481	        // on the `peer` component being distinct for concurrent peers.
   482	        // Verify same-counter different-peer FormatIdWires are not equal.
   483	        let a = FormatIdWire::Custom {
   484	            peer: PeerId::new(1),
   485	            counter: 7,
   486	        };
   487	        let b = FormatIdWire::Custom {
   488	            peer: PeerId::new(2),
   489	            counter: 7,
   490	        };
   491	        assert_ne!(a, b, "same counter, different peer must NOT collide");
   492	    }

   494	    #[test]
   495	    fn round_trips_worst_case_through_serde_json() {
   496	        // Renamed from `round_trips_through_loro_value_bincode` per
   497	        // Opus D-1 step 2 audit M2 — the test uses serde_json (which
   498	        // is the actual `Op` wire path: log.rs:94, 129 serialize via
   499	        // serde_json::to_string into Loro's LoroList values), not
   500	        // bincode or LoroValue's native binary format.
   501	        //
   502	        // FormatIdWire will live inside `Op::RegisterFormat` (step 4).
   503	        // The same JSON path that ops use must survive worst-case
   504	        // PeerId + counter values without overflow or truncation.
   505	        let original = FormatIdWire::Custom {
   506	            peer: PeerId::new(0xdead_beef_cafe_babe),

   508	        };
   509	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&original).unwrap();
   510	        let back: FormatIdWire = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
   511	        assert_eq!(back, original);
   512	    }

   515	    //
   516	    // `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` rejects payloads carrying fields
   517	    // the variant doesn't expect. The audit-locked rule "no fallbacks
   518	    // — errors must be visible" requires that producer bugs (writing
   519	    // an extra/misnamed field) fail loudly rather than silently drop
   520	    // the unknown data. The tests below pin the rejection contract so
   521	    // a future serde upgrade or accidental attribute removal can't
   522	    // weaken the schema.
   523	
   524	    #[test]
   525	    fn rejects_unknown_field_in_builtin_variant() {

   542	            result.is_err(),

   544	        );
   545	    }
   546	
   547	    #[test]
   548	    fn rejects_arbitrary_top_level_extra_field() {
   549	        // A producer that drifts the schema (e.g. adds `"comment":
   550	        // "..."` for human readability) must be rejected so we catch
   551	        // the drift before it lands in saved `.qbook` files.
   552	        let json = r#"{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"comment":"general format"}"#;
   553	        let result: Result<FormatIdWire, _> = serde_json::from_str(json);
   554	        assert!(
   555	            result.is_err(),

    pub fn register_at(&mut self, id: FormatId, s: &str) -> Result<(), FormatTableError> {
        // Step 1: id-side dedup. If `id` is already present, must map
        // to the same string (else IdCollision — a real corruption).
        if let Some(existing) = self.by_id.get(&id) {
            if existing == s {
                return Ok(());
            }
            return Err(FormatTableError::IdCollision {
                id,
                existing: existing.clone(),
                attempted: s.to_string(),
            });
        }
        // Step 2: string-side dedup, routed by variant.
        match id {
            FormatId::Builtin(_) => {
                if let Some(existing_id) = self.by_builtin_string.get(s) {
                    if *existing_id == id {
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    return Err(FormatTableError::StringCollision {
                        string: s.to_string(),
                        existing_id: *existing_id,
                        attempted_id: id,
                    });
                }
            }
            FormatId::Custom(peer, _) => {
                if let Some(existing_id) = self.by_custom_string.get(&(peer, s.to_string())) {
                    if *existing_id == id {
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    return Err(FormatTableError::StringCollision {
                        string: s.to_string(),
                        existing_id: *existing_id,
                        attempted_id: id,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        // Step 3: insert into by_id + the appropriate string map.
        self.by_id.insert(id, s.to_string());
        match id {
            FormatId::Builtin(_) => {
                self.by_builtin_string.insert(s.to_string(), id);
            }
            FormatId::Custom(peer, _) => {
                self.by_custom_string.insert((peer, s.to_string()), id);
            }
        }
        // Step 4: if `id` is a Custom-variant for OUR peer, advance
        // the local counter so subsequent `intern` calls allocate
        // fresh counters past any replayed ones.
        if let FormatId::Custom(peer, counter) = id {
            if peer == self.local_peer && counter >= self.next_custom_counter {
                self.next_custom_counter = counter + 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Total entries — useful for sanity checks, not for hot paths.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.by_id.len()
    }

    /// True iff the table has no entries (should only be possible if a
    /// caller clears it; default construction loads built-ins).
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.by_id.is_empty()
    }

quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-13-cross-sheet-references.md:45:**Codex HIGH-1 revision.** The first draft of this section proposed "SheetId is canonical at every layer below the parser; sheet names live only at lex/parse and print/serialize." Codex identified the split-brain: `Op::PutFormula` and `.qbook/sheets/N.jsonl` persist RAW FORMULA TEXT with sheet names. After a rename, the in-memory plan uses the new name but persisted text uses the old name; on reload / cache miss / recompute-from-text, the parser sees the stale name and errors.

quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:551:### 12.2 .qbook persistence — save-side spill-target skip
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:553:Codex HIGH: the original "no schema bump because computed overlay round-trips" claim was false. Current `.qbook` save emits non-formula non-blank cells as user-overlay records (see `qbook_format.rs` save loop). If a spill produces values at A2..A5 (from `=SEQUENCE(5)` at A1), those cells currently have no formula but have computed-overlay values. On reload (without spill anchor awareness), each non-formula cell record gets routed to USER overlay, which would then BLOCK the anchor at re-recompute time.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:566:**Edge case:** a `.qbook` saved by a pre-W5-105 reader (no skip logic) WOULD include the spill-target cells as user records. On load, recompute_all re-evaluates the formula, sees the user blocker(s), and emits `#SPILL!` at the anchor. This is a regression for "saved-before-fix files loaded after-fix" — documented as a known transitional gap, not a closure-blocker.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:673:A `.qbook` saved by pre-W5-105 code (no skip logic per § 12.2) contains spill-target cells as user-overlay records. Post-W5-105 load → recompute_all sees user blockers → emits `#SPILL!` at the anchor. Documented transitional gap; not a closure-blocker.

quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:160:6. **Table footprint fits within the Excel address grid** — NEW W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 closure, Codex HIGH-1). `top_row + rows - 1` must be `≤ MAX_ROW` (1,048,575) and `top_col + cols - 1` must be `≤ MAX_COLUMN` (16,383). `TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds` (in `ql-storage`) is the shared check; called at FIVE entry points: producer `create_table` / `resize_table`, replay `apply_create_table` / `apply_resize_table`, and v6 `.qbook` loader. Pre-W5-125 the check was missing, so `for r in top_row..top_row + rows` either ran past the addressable grid (registering cells later `Sheet::put` would panic on) or u32-overflowed silently (skipping all downstream overlap / spill-anchor checks).

quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:52:| ~~GAP-S-01~~ | ~~Single overlay per chunk (user + formula outputs share state)~~ — **CLOSED** in Engine Phase 3.5 (commit-after-645c7baf3bf, W5-38). `ColumnStore` now carries parallel `user_overlays` + `computed_overlays` per chunk; read cascade is user → computed → base; `put` (user) clears computed at the row, `put_computed` clears user. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:176:### I. Schema v5 / `.qbook` Format
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:179:`crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs:119` sets version to `5`. `MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` at line 127. Version gate at load time (`qbook_format.rs:1222–1228`) enforces `1 ≤ found ≤ 5`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:182:`qbook_format.rs:362–377`: `scope: Option<u16>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. v1-v4 payloads load correctly with `scope: None`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:188:`qbook_format.rs:1012–1041`: iterates workbook-scoped names (scope: None), then per-sheet scoped names (scope: Some(sheet_id)). Sorted by `(scope, name)` for deterministic diffs. Correct.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:191:`qbook_format.rs:1431–1458`: `scope: None` → `wb.set_name(...)`, `scope: Some(sheet_id)` → `wb.sheet_mut(sheet_id).set_scoped_name(...)`. Unknown `sheet_id` surfaces as `MalformedName`. Correct.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:197:`qbook_format.rs:1222–1228` rejects `schema_version > 5` (or, from a v4 reader's perspective, `> 4`). The version gate is the primary safety net. The secondary safety (`serde(default)` + `deny_unknown_fields` — not present on `NamedEntry`) is a gap (I.3 above) but not a regression from v4.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:11:The doc says formulas survive rename because AST/plans carry SheetId, while `Op::PutFormula` and `.qbook` formula cells still persist raw formula text containing sheet names. That is a split-brain contract. A workbook can parse `Sheet2!A1`, store an AST/plan with `sheet = 1`, rename sheet 1 to `Data`, and continue evaluating from a cached plan. But the persisted formula text is still `Sheet2!A1` unless rename rewrites formula sources. On reload, replay, cache miss, or recompute after cache invalidation, eager parse will see `Sheet2` as unknown and fail.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:16:- or `.qbook`/op-log persist a resolved formula representation alongside display text;
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:21:HIGH-2: Extending v4 in place contradicts the current qbook compatibility policy.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:65:MEDIUM-4: `SetSheetScopedName` as a separate op risks schema drift from `.qbook` names.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:67:The doc proposes `NamedEntry.scope` in `.qbook` but a separate `Op::SetSheetScopedName` in the op log. That can work, but it creates two representations for the same concept. A simpler and less divergent shape is `Op::SetName { scope: Option<SheetId>, name, target }` in a new op-log schema/version, mirroring the v5 qbook `NamedEntry`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:123:A -> B -> C -> D is close, but the real first deliverable should be "sheet registry API and canonicalizer" before parser work. Parser context, rename collision checks, printer inverse lookup, qbook load validation, and IDE diagnostics all depend on that. Sheet-scoped names can land after rename only if the rename design already accounts for per-sheet name tables and cache generations.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:133:Schema bump policy: HIGH. New `scope` field requires qbook schema v5 under the current `deny_unknown_fields` policy.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:150:2. Change qbook persistence decision from "extend v4 in place" to "schema v5; v1-v4 load as workbook-scoped names."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:155:7. Align op-log and qbook name scope shapes, preferably with `scope: Option<SheetId>` in both persisted surfaces after explicit version bumps.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-codex.md:6429:Detail: The docs define `Builtin` as `0..=163`, but the public enum allows `FormatId::Builtin(200)`, and tests currently register it. `to_legacy_u32()` returns `Some(200)`, while `is_custom()` is false, so qbook/xlsx custom-format rosters skip the string at save/export (`qbook_format.rs:1192`, `umya_export.rs:347`). That can produce overlays or XLSX style ids with no persisted format definition.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-3-codex.md:6434:Detail: Repo production paths still default to `LEGACY_PEER`; searches show non-legacy `with_peer` usage only in `ql-storage` tests. But `FormatTable::with_peer` / `set_local_peer` are public, so step 3 does allow non-LEGACY `FormatId`s before the qbook/op/xlsx schemas can carry them. Runtime append, qbook save, and xlsx export can panic if that API is used early.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:336:- **XS-4-04** — Op-log + `.qbook` persistence preserve sheet identity through round-trips.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:359:- **Sheet-scoped names:** `NameTable` is workbook-flat. The wire format `NamedTargetWire` (in `ql-io::qbook_format`) has no scope field. `WorkbookEnv::lookup_name` is workbook-scope only.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:366:**Codex HIGH-1 revision.** The first draft of this section proposed "SheetId is canonical at every layer below the parser; sheet names live only at lex/parse and print/serialize." Codex identified the split-brain: `Op::PutFormula` and `.qbook/sheets/N.jsonl` persist RAW FORMULA TEXT with sheet names. After a rename, the in-memory plan uses the new name but persisted text uses the old name; on reload / cache miss / recompute-from-text, the parser sees the stale name and errors.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:371:- **Persisted formula text** (`Op::PutFormula.text`, `Workbook::formula_cells`, `.qbook/sheets/N.jsonl`): canonical by sheet NAME. **Sheet rename rewrites all stored formula text** so on-disk source stays parseable. Matches Excel canon (rename in Excel rewrites every formula in the workbook that references the renamed sheet).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:406:- Binder, planner, runtime, op log, .qbook envelope, calcgraph — all store `SheetId`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:412:Trade-off: text-only contexts (raw `.qbook` JSONL, xlsx files we don't fully own yet) carry the SHEET NAME (not id) in formula source. The qbook loader already re-parses formula text at load time (via Phase 2B.3 PlanCache); rebinding happens automatically as long as the name map is current.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7-design-codex-review.txt:8879:12. FLAG - HIGH: The “no schema bump because computed overlay round-trips” claim is false for spill targets. Current qbook save emits non-formula nonblank cells as ordinary records, and load routes non-formula records to the user overlay; persisted spill targets would reload as blockers and turn the anchor into `#SPILL!`. Fix by either skipping derived spill-target cells during save and recomputing them on load, or bumping schema to persist value lane / spill metadata explicitly.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1791:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

Verify by reading `crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs` for the actual constant + checking that step 5's loader will consume `from_u32_legacy(n)` for ALL u32 values present in old `.qbook` files — including the rare cases like `n = u32::MAX` (which step 2 doesn't test). Today: `RegisterFormat { id: u32, string: String }`. Step 4 will change `id: u32 → id: FormatIdWire`. Is the surrounding code (replay handlers, producer sites) structured such that the migration is clean? Any sites that observe `id: u32` numerically that would break under a tagged-enum?

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:8828:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1791:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:10413:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:619:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:10619:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11418:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID.
