quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2466:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:720:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2550:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:854:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2552:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:856:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2586:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:900:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-prompt.md:42:- `crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs` — `WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION 4 → 5`, `NamedEntry.scope: Option<u16>` with serde-default + skip_serializing_if, save-side scope collection + sort, load-side route-by-scope + `MalformedName` for unknown sheet id, `future_schema_version_rejected` bumped to v6.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2686:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1049:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:338:If `Workbook::formula_at` returned `Some(Arc::from(""))` (an empty string), `formula_text_at` would return `Some("=")`. FORMULATEXT(A1) would return `Value::Text("=")`. Today the empty-formula state is unreachable: `set_formula` would lex+parse-fail on empty input; `put_formula` raw is internal-test-only in product paths. But `Workbook::put_formula` is `pub`, and a future code path or external integration (e.g., `ql-io` reading a corrupted `.qbook/` formula table) could land an empty string.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3932:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1596:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:339:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3935:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1599:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:454:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:4344:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:338:If `Workbook::formula_at` returned `Some(Arc::from(""))` (an empty string), `formula_text_at` would return `Some("=")`. Today the empty-formula state is unreachable: `set_formula` would lex+parse-fail on empty input; `put_formula` raw is internal-test-only in product paths. But `Workbook::put_formula` is `pub`, and a future code path or external integration (e.g., `ql-io` reading a corrupted `.qbook/` formula table) could land an empty string.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:4:Scope per the design doc (`docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-design.md` §97-112): cross-crate dependency map, public-API stability per crate, error taxonomy across crates, `.qbook` persistence forward/back compat, test architecture across crates, crate build hygiene, documentation coherence. Out of scope: function correctness (Codex), cross-feature integration (Opus-A), defensive/fuzz (Opus-B), audit-trail (self).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:12:**Phase 4 is structurally ready to enter Phase 5 (CRDT collaboration) — but not without three things landing first.** The architectural decisions taken in Phase 0-1 (T1-D02 hand-rolled graph, T1-D05 Loro reserved-for-oplog, T2-D01 `.qbook/` directory) have held under 11 sub-phases of feature pressure and the dependency graph remains acyclic. The 24-crate workspace shape has not needed to bend.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:20:3. **Persistence format magic-byte / version-probe symmetry between `.qbook/workbook.toml` and `oplog.bin`**. `.qbook/` has a v1-7 ladder with a two-phase probe; `oplog.bin` is a raw Loro `ExportMode::Snapshot` blob with no engine-level versioning. Phase 5's "merge two oplogs" semantics will need a version field. See HIGH-4.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:26:- `.qbook/` schema versioning: v1 → v7 migration ladder, fail-loud on `UnsupportedSchema`, deny-unknown-fields strictness — well-shaped.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:62:| ql-io | `QbookError` | `qbook_format.rs:185` | 14 |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:118:- `ql-io` is the file-format crate (`.qbook/` directory + TOML envelope + JSONL sheets). The "Wire" suffix on `CellWireValue` was named for the file-wire representation — serde-friendly, NaN/Inf-rejecting, schema-versioned.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:124:- A future change to `.qbook/` wire format (say, adding `CellWireValue::Date(i64)`) breaks the op-log mutation set, even if no `.qbook/` files are involved.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:125:- Phase 5 CRDT merge needs to evolve `Op` independently of file format — today every op-log evolution forces a `.qbook/` schema bump.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:132:### HIGH-4 — `oplog.bin` has no engine-level magic bytes / version field
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:136:Compared to `.qbook/` (which has a clean `schema_version: u32` ladder v1..=v7 with a two-phase probe per `crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs:386-395`), the op-log has:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:154:`OpLog::export_bytes` prepends this header; `OpLog::import_bytes` parses + validates. Forward-compat: a v1 reader seeing v2 returns `OpLogError::UnsupportedSchema { found: 2 }` rather than a Loro-internal decode error. Backward-compat: a v2 writer can emit v1-format when no v2-specific feature is in use (per `.qbook/` precedent at `qbook_format.rs:1359-1382`).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:235:- `ql-oplog` drops its `ql-io` dependency (verified: `grep -rn "use ql_io" crates/ql-oplog/src/` shows zero non-persistence-module uses; only `persistence.rs` needs `ql_io::{load_workbook, save_workbook_extending, QbookError}`, and that can become a separate `ql-oplog-persistence` sub-module or stay).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:324:### MEDIUM-9 — `WorkbookEnvelope` schema bump cadence is healthy but `oplog.bin` is not similarly versioned
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:326:The `.qbook/workbook.toml` envelope has migrated v1 → v7 across Phases 2A-4.9 with proper additive-field serde defaults, two-phase loader probe, and explicit `ForwardCompatFieldOnOldVersion` error path (`qbook_format.rs:319-325`). This is exemplary.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:328:`oplog.bin` (per HIGH-4) has no analogous ladder. The Phase 5 CRDT redesign will need the same forward/backward compat shape. Today the only "version" signal is `OpLogError::SchemaMismatch(&'static str)` with hard-coded messages.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:330:**Recommendation:** combined with HIGH-4, treat `oplog.bin` schema versioning as a Phase 5 prep deliverable. The same two-phase pattern (version probe → full deserialize) applied at `OpLog::import_bytes`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:510:`crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs:160, 168`:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:518:Compare `.zip`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`: those formats have explicit "minimum reader" policies. `.qbook/` does not.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:545:### `.qbook/` directory format
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:547:**Shape:** TOML envelope (`workbook.toml`) + per-sheet JSONL (`sheets/N.jsonl`) + optional `oplog.bin` + atomic-save marker (`.atomic-save-marker-v1`).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:555:### `oplog.bin` (Loro snapshot)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:561:**Verdict:** **NOT ready for v2.** Phase 5 will reshape the op model (CRDT merge needs peer-aware ops). With no magic-bytes / version-probe at the wrapping level, evolution is harder than `.qbook/` — every change requires either a Loro container rename (`OPS_CONTAINER` per `log.rs:34`) or breaking the on-disk format.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1724:docs/MASTER-PLAN.md:69:Phase 2A closed a large correctness and persistence pass: defined names, transactions, load-and-recompute, dotted function identifiers, schema v2, crash-safe save, Excel-canon coercion fixes, deterministic formula fingerprints, error ergonomics, and audit closure. Phase 2A.3 then shipped Loro-backed op-log scaffolding: `ql-oplog`, typed `Op` variants, Loro snapshot persistence, replay, runtime and transaction producer wiring, and `.qbook/oplog.bin` persistence. The stale `docs/phase2/entry-plan.md` and `docs/phase2/exit-packet.md` still say 2A.3 is deferred; this plan supersedes that statement and requires a doc-rot repair pass in Phase 2B.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1827:docs/phase2/entry-plan.md:7:> **STALE BANNER (added 2026-05-12 end-of-day):** This document was written when Phase 2A.3 (op log) was still deferred. Since then, 2A.3 has shipped in three commits: `dfc2a9900ef` (scaffolding) + `a6de4b4a50b` (runtime/transaction wiring) + `fc977815cd2` (`oplog.bin` persistence). The canonical engine plan is now `docs/MASTER-PLAN.md`. New sessions: read MASTER-PLAN.md first. This file remains for historical context of the Phase 2A roadmap.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1832:docs/phase2/entry-plan.md:189:**Tests** (6 in `loader::tests`): formula refresh against stale-on-disk values, formula-free workbook, missing-path load error, empty workbook, multiple formulas all recomputed, named-range round-trip pins the persistence gap (`.qbook` doesn't yet serialize `NameTable`; load surfaces `Recompute(UnresolvedName)` — flagged for Phase 2B+).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2102:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:160:6. **Table footprint fits within the Excel address grid** — NEW W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 closure, Codex HIGH-1). `top_row + rows - 1` must be `≤ MAX_ROW` (1,048,575) and `top_col + cols - 1` must be `≤ MAX_COLUMN` (16,383). `TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds` (in `ql-storage`) is the shared check; called at FIVE entry points: producer `create_table` / `resize_table`, replay `apply_create_table` / `apply_resize_table`, and v6 `.qbook` loader. Pre-W5-125 the check was missing, so `for r in top_row..top_row + rows` either ran past the addressable grid (registering cells later `Sheet::put` would panic on) or u32-overflowed silently (skipping all downstream overlap / spill-anchor checks).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2257:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2292:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:171:| TEXT | ✅ | 28 | 4.5.E | W5-83: render Value via parsed Excel format string. Built on the W5-77→W5-82 format module (parser+renderer+FormatTable+overlay+runtime). Parse failures (incl. V2-deferred [Red]/conditionals/elapsed/fraction) surface as #VALUE!. Tests in `format::text_fn::tests` + `workbook_runtime::tests::text_formula_*` + e2e `format_persistence_round_trip_through_qbook`. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2323:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:132:**Persistence round-trip (OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS PHASE):** `register_spill` then save+load round-trip is deferred to Phase 4.7.L per design § 7.3. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:720:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:854:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:856:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:900:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-prompt.md:42:- `crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs` — `WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION 4 → 5`, `NamedEntry.scope: Option<u16>` with serde-default + skip_serializing_if, save-side scope collection + sort, load-side route-by-scope + `MalformedName` for unknown sheet id, `future_schema_version_rejected` bumped to v6.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1049:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:338:If `Workbook::formula_at` returned `Some(Arc::from(""))` (an empty string), `formula_text_at` would return `Some("=")`. FORMULATEXT(A1) would return `Value::Text("=")`. Today the empty-formula state is unreachable: `set_formula` would lex+parse-fail on empty input; `put_formula` raw is internal-test-only in product paths. But `Workbook::put_formula` is `pub`, and a future code path or external integration (e.g., `ql-io` reading a corrupted `.qbook/` formula table) could land an empty string.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1599:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:454:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:14:**M1 — `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` missing on `FormatIdWire`.** Verified empirically: `{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"extra":1}` deserializes silently to `Builtin { id: 14 }`. `qbook_format.rs:561, 571` already uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `FormatEntry` / `FormatOverlayEntry` for exactly this protection. `NamedTargetWire` (wire.rs:137-139) lacks it too — likely a pre-existing gap rather than a step-2-introduced regression — but `FormatIdWire` going on the wire in step 4 makes the gap newly load-bearing. Either add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `FormatIdWire` now, or document the decision (alongside `NamedTargetWire`) that wire types accept extra fields for forward-compat. Per the global "No Fallbacks" rule, silent acceptance of unknown fields is the kind of soft failure that masks producer bugs.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:20:**L1 — `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX` not `pub`.** wire.rs:295 keeps the const file-private. Step 5 (qbook envelope loader) and step 6 (xlsx export at `umya_export.rs`) both will want a shared boundary value. Two options: (a) export `pub const FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX` (or `FIRST_XLSX_CUSTOM_NUMFMT = 164`) from `ql_oplog::wire`, OR (b) defer — duplicate the const in step 5/6 callers and audit then. Either works; (a) is mildly cleaner because the d-1-checklist already names `FIRST_XLSX_CUSTOM_NUMFMT` as a shared concept. Not blocking step 3 (step 3 has no use for this constant).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:22:**L2 — No `is_builtin` / `is_custom` / `peer` / `counter` accessors.** Step 3's storage `FormatId` will mirror this shape, and the many `id.0 >= FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID` discriminators (qbook_format.rs:1179; ql-io-xlsx tests at 68, 115, 49, 169, 229, 400, 766, 264, 769, 887 — 10+ sites) become `is_custom()` calls at step 3. Adding `is_builtin` / `is_custom` here in step 2 would be premature (the storage type owns those once it mirrors the shape); deferring to step 3 is fine. Document either way.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-opus.md:34:- No arithmetic on `Op::RegisterFormat.id: u32` or `Op::SetCellFormat.id: Option<u32>` in replay (replay.rs:497-540) or producer (formats.rs:41-114) — only `==` / `lookup` lookups + `>= FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID` filter at save (qbook_format.rs:1179). Step 4 swap is a clean signature change at these sites; step 5 reads the filter through `from_u32_legacy`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:36:| `.bak-<random>` recovery scans by filename prefix — could nuke user `book.qbook.bak-2025-review` | ✓ |   |   |   |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:58:**Codex finding.** `recover_from_crashed_save` (`qbook_format.rs:610`) iterates `<basename>.bak-*` siblings and either deletes them (target valid) or renames them over the target (target missing). A legitimate user-created backup like `book.qbook.bak-2025-review` next to `book.qbook` is treated as an orphan and either deleted or — worse — installed as the workbook.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:63:**Codex finding.** `Workbook::put_formula` (`workbook.rs:293`) accepts any (sheet, row, col) without bounds checking. The 2A.7 H1 fix added `validate_cell` at the runtime/transaction layer, but a caller reaching directly into `Workbook::put_formula` (the qbook loader is the prod caller) bypasses it. Downstream `recompute_all`'s `put_at` would panic on bad coords.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:65:**Fix**: make `Workbook::put_formula` return `Result<(), InvalidCell>` and validate row/col internally. Or document the invariant + assert at debug-build time. Loader already pre-validates row/col bounds (qbook_format.rs:911-924), so this is defense-in-depth + future-proofing.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:73:**Agent A finding.** `qbook_format.rs:929-947`: the rule `is_v1 && rec.formula.is_some() && rec.value == Error("#NULL!")` matches BOTH:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:82:**Agent A finding.** `save_workbook` (`qbook_format.rs:485-487`) calls `fs::rename(path, &paths.backup)` when `path.exists()`. If `path` is a regular file (no enforcement of `.qbook` suffix being a directory), the rename succeeds, the file becomes `.bak-<random>`, recovery on next load tries `remove_dir_all` on it (errors cleanly via `eprintln!`), and the user's pre-existing regular file ends up orphaned.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:327:**Codex HIGH-1 revision.** The first draft of this section proposed "SheetId is canonical at every layer below the parser; sheet names live only at lex/parse and print/serialize." Codex identified the split-brain: `Op::PutFormula` and `.qbook/sheets/N.jsonl` persist RAW FORMULA TEXT with sheet names. After a rename, the in-memory plan uses the new name but persisted text uses the old name; on reload / cache miss / recompute-from-text, the parser sees the stale name and errors.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:332:- **Persisted formula text** (`Op::PutFormula.text`, `Workbook::formula_cells`, `.qbook/sheets/N.jsonl`): canonical by sheet NAME. **Sheet rename rewrites all stored formula text** so on-disk source stays parseable. Matches Excel canon (rename in Excel rewrites every formula in the workbook that references the renamed sheet).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:367:- Binder, planner, runtime, op log, .qbook envelope, calcgraph — all store `SheetId`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:373:Trade-off: text-only contexts (raw `.qbook` JSONL, xlsx files we don't fully own yet) carry the SHEET NAME (not id) in formula source. The qbook loader already re-parses formula text at load time (via Phase 2B.3 PlanCache); rebinding happens automatically as long as the name map is current.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:554:## 9. Decision F — Persistence (`.qbook`)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:566:`Op::RenameSheet` events live in the op log. Loading a `.qbook` with an attached `oplog.bin` replays the rename history; the final state matches what was saved. No new persistence surface beyond the op-log variant.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:657:- **R-E:** Sheet rename + op-log replay determinism. If a `.qbook` snapshot is saved AFTER a rename and the op-log replayed against a fresh empty workbook, the snapshot's `Sheet::name` and the op-log's `RenameSheet` events both need to converge. **Mitigation:** snapshot is authoritative for sheet names; op-log replay applies AFTER snapshot is loaded (current `load_workbook_and_recompute` order).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-opus.md:32:- **LEGACY_PEER deferral defensible.** D-1 checklist locates the sentinel at step 5 (qbook envelope schema bump) where its only call-site (the legacy-u32 loader) is born. Adding the constant in step 1 with no consumer would (a) violate the no-unused-symbols hygiene the project enforces and (b) prematurely commit to one of two equally-valid encodings (`PeerId(0)` vs `PeerId(u64::MAX - 1)`). The checklist explicitly hedges "Pick one in step 1" but the decision criterion (Loro acceptance, sentinel collision avoidance) is more naturally informed by step 5's loader needs. Defer is correct.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:627:### CC-5 — Export/import (qbook round-trip).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:629:The design v2 § 5.5 / § 8 R7 (new) says qbook round-trips formulas as source text via `Workbook::formula_at`. Step 1 doesn't change this; FORMULATEXT (Step 4) prepends `=` at the function boundary. No serialization concerns.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:619:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-codex.md:11400:  `intern_format` predicts `next_custom_id` before logging (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:51`). Two peers from the same base can both emit `RegisterFormat { id: N, string: different }`. Replay calls `register_at` (`crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:451`), and `register_at` rejects same id/different string as `IdCollision` (`crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:129`). Cleanest fix: make custom format ids globally unique, e.g. `Builtin(u32) | Custom { peer_id, counter }` or a widened `u128`/UUID. Wire impact: `RegisterFormat.id`, `SetCellFormat.id`, `FormatId(pub u32)`, and persisted qbook/xlsx mapping need a schema bump or compatibility layer.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:4163:docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-c.md:561:**Verdict:** **NOT ready for v2.** Phase 5 will reshape the op model (CRDT merge needs peer-aware ops). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-tier-c1-codex.md:8976:  Spill-target producer-alias cycles are only detected if spill anchors already exist when `rebuild_from_workbook` runs. `.qbook` load intentionally does not restore spill state (`crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs:3480`), while producer-alias extraction depends on `workbook.spill_target_anchor` (`crates/ql-exec/src/calcgraph_session.rs:724`). Dynamic cycles through re-derived spill targets can therefore be missed on cold load.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:339:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:342:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:123:A -> B -> C -> D is close, but the real first deliverable should be "sheet registry API and canonicalizer" before parser work. Parser context, rename collision checks, printer inverse lookup, qbook load validation, and IDE diagnostics all depend on that. Sheet-scoped names can land after rename only if the rename design already accounts for per-sheet name tables and cache generations.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:343:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:133:Schema bump policy: HIGH. New `scope` field requires qbook schema v5 under the current `deny_unknown_fields` policy.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:454:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:455:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:197:`qbook_format.rs:1222–1228` rejects `schema_version > 5` (or, from a v4 reader's perspective, `> 4`). The version gate is the primary safety net. The secondary safety (`serde(default)` + `deny_unknown_fields` — not present on `NamedEntry`) is a gap (I.3 above) but not a regression from v4.

  - ql-io: qbook envelope save/load uses `to_legacy_u32().expect(...)` + `is_custom()`. Pre-step-5 envelope still u32-shaped.

- ✅ Verified: 4244 workspace tests passing (+7 from new tests); fmt + clippy clean; no truncation.

### Step 4: Update `Op::RegisterFormat` / `Op::SetCellFormat` to use FormatIdWire (1-2 hours)

- Wire-format bump in Op enum.
- Update producer (`ql-exec::workbook_runtime::formats`) + replay (`ql-oplog::replay`) to use the new shape.
- Tests update.
- Commit: `Phase 5.2 D-1 step 4 — Op wire format uses FormatIdWire`.

### Step 5: Backwards-compat in `qbook_format` (2-3 hours)

- Schema version bump.
- Old-format loader: detect schema version, migrate `u32` → `FormatId` via legacy mapping.
- Tests: load a fixture saved at the old schema, verify successful migration.
- Commit: `Phase 5.2 D-1 step 5 — qbook envelope schema bump + legacy loader`.

### Step 6: xlsx export / import (1-2 hours)

- Flatten `FormatId` → xlsx `numFmtId` on export.
- Inflate xlsx `numFmtId` → `FormatId::Builtin(n)` on import.
- Tests: existing xlsx round-trip tests should pass.
- Commit: `Phase 5.2 D-1 step 6 — xlsx numFmtId ↔ FormatId mapping`.

### Step 7: Tier D3 — oplog.bin magic bytes + version header (1 hour)

- Bundle with D-1 per the entry plan. Add a 4-byte magic header + u32 schema version to `oplog.bin`.
- This is the discriminator the loader uses to know whether to apply legacy FormatId migration.
- Commit: `Tier D3 — oplog.bin magic bytes + schema version header`.

### Step 8: Audit (mandatory per discipline rule)

- 2-way Codex + Opus audit of the full D-1 arc. Multi-step schema change is exactly the kind of cycle the audit-discipline rule was written for.

[HIGH] `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` still dedupes strings globally.
File:Line: [formats.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:45)
Detail: This line scans `FormatTable::iter()` and returns the first matching string, but step 4 made duplicate strings legal across peer custom namespaces and across Builtin/Custom. If local peer A has replayed `Custom(B,0) = "yyyy-mm-dd"`, runtime `intern_format("yyyy-mm-dd")` returns B’s id and emits no `RegisterFormat`, while `FormatTable::intern` would allocate `Custom(A,0)`. After the LibreOffice `Custom(LEGACY,0) = "General"` case, this can also bypass builtin-first precedence because `HashMap` iteration is unordered.
Recommendation: fix now

Detail: Step 4 makes arbitrary `FormatIdWire::Custom { counter: u32 }` reachable through op replay. Registering `Custom(local_peer, u32::MAX)` makes `counter + 1` overflow in debug builds and wrap to `0` in release; `set_local_peer` has the same pattern at [format.rs:310](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:310), and `intern` can also overflow at [format.rs:347](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:347). Release wrap can later overwrite or reuse lower counters.

[HIGH] `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` still dedupes strings globally.
File:Line: [formats.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime/formats.rs:45)
Detail: This line scans `FormatTable::iter()` and returns the first matching string, but step 4 made duplicate strings legal across peer custom namespaces and across Builtin/Custom. If local peer A has replayed `Custom(B,0) = "yyyy-mm-dd"`, runtime `intern_format("yyyy-mm-dd")` returns B’s id and emits no `RegisterFormat`, while `FormatTable::intern` would allocate `Custom(A,0)`. After the LibreOffice `Custom(LEGACY,0) = "General"` case, this can also bypass builtin-first precedence because `HashMap` iteration is unordered.
Recommendation: fix now
